note: Provenance for the landing page's product material. Staleness in a capture is invisible in review — the old gallery shipped a v0.0.42beta window with an empty Mission Board and a stray text selection for weeks. Recording what each asset was captured from makes the gap a fact instead of an impression. test/lander-assets.test.ts asserts this file agrees with both src/assets/lander and public/media, whose files are listed here under a media/ prefix.

refresh.gallery: Run the desktop app on the target release, drive it to the state each shot describes, and capture the window. Shots must show real work, not an empty state.
refresh.conceptFlow: qa/record-real-client-demo.ps1 records the desktop window against a live task, then qa/curate-client-demo.mjs edits the frames into the GIF.
refresh.demoVideo: Record the desktop app driving one real task end to end, then re-encode for the web: ffmpeg -i <capture> -an -c:v libx264 -profile:v high -level 4.0 -preset slow -crf 28 -pix_fmt yuv420p -g 60 -movflags +faststart public/media/opencorvus-demo.mp4. -an drops the capture's silent system-audio channel and +faststart puts the moov atom in front, without which a browser must download the whole file before the first frame. The poster is one frame of the same file: ffmpeg -ss <t> -i <mp4> -frames:v 1 -q:v 4 <poster>.jpg. The README cannot show that file playing: GitHub renders an inline player only for its own user-attachments uploads, and a raw URL to a committed .mp4 is served as an attachment, so it downloads. media/opencorvus-demo.gif is the excerpt that does autoplay there — two beats cut from the same recording: ffmpeg -ss 15.5 -t 9 and -ss 42.5 -t 9, concat, then fps=12,scale=900:-1,palettegen(max_colors=128,stats_mode=diff) + paletteuse(dither=bayer). Keep it under a few megabytes; GitHub proxies README images through camo.
